scope: Proposition 7.4 (Simultaneous disjoint domains) of the manuscript “A torsion-free counterexample to reduced Baum–Connes injectivity” (preprints/A-Torsion-Free-Counterexample-to-Reduced-Baum-Connes-Injectivity-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 285 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 df8d9301aa6d0306), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 63. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are sets RQ ⊆ V (Q), one for each sheet, such that each RQ is empty, an old-centered ball BQ(v), or a private singleton, and the sets DQ = V (Q) \ RQ have the following properties. 1. The physical vertex sets DQ are pairwise disjoint. 2. Put Eint = [ Q∈Q {e ∈ E(Q) : both endpoints of e lie in DQ}. Every edge in this union has a unique such sheet, and (V (C), E(C) \ Eint) is a forest. 3. StarQ(RQ) is a forest. If RQ contains an old vertex of layer i, then |RQ| ≤ 210Hi . A private singleton removes no old coordinate. No equivariance of the choices RQ is asserted or needed.
